chunks: Al-Husayn from Fadalah from Saif from Abu Bakr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
My father asked him, and I was listening, about the limit of the illness in which fasting is left unperformed, so he said: 'When he is unable to perform suhur (pre-dawn meal).'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific condition of illness that exempts a Muslim from fasting according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a practical physiological threshold for breaking the fast: the inability to perform *suhur* (pre-dawn meal) due to weakness. This criterion highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the capacity to fulfill the ritual's foundational elements as the primary indicator of valid exemption, rather than mere general fatigue. It underscores the balance between religious obligation and ease (*rukhas*) in cases of illness.
